title: bundle-arbitrage-capacity-curves
summary: Working spreadsheet + narrative for evaluating bundle arbitrage across capacity curves: compares appliance-heavy on-prem amortization to VPC subscription with tiered licensing and support bundles. Focused on mid-sized customers (10k-200k qps-equivalent monthly tokens) and variable SLA/support mixes.
assumptions: HW amortized over 36 months for appliances; 60 months considered for chassis-heavy buys
Average token throughput equivalence mapped to QPS baseline via internal benchmark (qps = tokens/50 on gen workloads)
Power + rack + ops headcount included in OpEx by a blended multiplier (1.15x of raw infra cost)
Support bundles priced as percent of license: basic=15%, premium=30%, enterprise=50%
Network egress/transfer included as variable monthly line item for VPC scenarios (estimated at $0.08/GB)
Quantization/efficiency tuning reduces GPU count by ~20% for compatible models; savings shown in scenarios
scenarios: Lean-Edge: small on-prem appliance (2x A10GR), annual support basic, modest throughput
Dedicated-Peak: large on-prem rack (8x A100-equivalent), premium support, high throughput, ops team
VPC-Standard: cloud reserved instance + managed control plane, license per qps tier, basic support
Hybrid-Burst: on-prem baseline + VPC burst for peak 30% traffic, enterprise support, license crosswalk applied

calc_notes: Amortized_capex applied at chassis level; include refresh tax of 8% to account for unexpected replacements
Ops multiplier applied to on-prem power/rack (includes facilities, cooling, 2 FTEs per 100k qps equivalent)
Sensitivity knobs in sheet: quantization_percent, model_seq_length_delta, reserved_commit_discount
BreakevenMonths computed vs VPC baseline using NPV with discount rate 6% (quick comparison mode uses straight months)
License crosswalk: per-qps tiers assume stepped pricing; verify with sales for enterprise NegotiatedDyson adjustments
recommended_action: Ship a trimmed appendix to Sales and Solutions: 1) add a per-customer profile page with their measured qps/token mix + expected seq length, 2) run sensitivity for 10%, 25%, 50% quantization savings, 3) flag customers where support-tier arbitrage flips decision (ie. on-prem cheaper only if basic support accepted). Draft also suggests creating two standard bundle SKUs: Bundle-A (on-prem-friendly amortization rebate) and Bundle-B (VPC commit discount) to simplify quoting.

Confirm whether premium support includes guaranteed model tuning time (adds 0.5 FTE equivalent to cost)
